title: Jeroboam never denied Jehovah—calf-cult was relative, referred to him, and still branded gravest idolatry
source_text: XL. Adde quod Jeroboam, dum vitulos conflavit, ut essent divinitatis symbola quae populus adoraret, non ideo negavit Jehovam esse verum Deum, nec alium Deum populo proposuit. Unde sequitur, cultum illum relativum fuisse, & ad Jehovam referri: qui tamen cultus in Scriptura tanquam idololatria gravissima damnatur. Quod evidens argumentum est, non solum absolutam, sed etiam relativam imaginum adorationem lege divina prohiberi.
pass_a_gloss: Add that Jeroboam, while he cast the calves that they might be symbols of divinity which the people would adore, did not therefore deny that Jehovah is the true God, nor propose another God to the people. Whence it follows that that cult was relative, and referred to Jehovah: which cult yet is condemned in Scripture as most grave idolatry. Which is an evident argument that not only absolute, but also relative adoration of images is prohibited by divine law.
pass_b_english: No rival deity was preached—only Jehovah via calf-symbols.
Scripture’s idolatry verdict on that relative cult proves the law bans relative image-adoration too.

choices.why: Punchline for relative as well as absolute.
